spec.title: codkit PROP-014: The standards package and licence markup

status.comment: standalone contract: the standards package in the tool root, the licence markup check, delivery of the package into the product repository; revision 1 (campaign STANDARDS, 2026-09-06)

p.STD-PURPOSE: Codkit ships a **standards package** — a vibe package of kind `flow` with norms for a patch-set repository — and can deliver it into a product repository with `codkit standards load`, so that an ordinary `vibe install` materializes it from there. Every file of the package carries machine-readable licence information, and it is checked algorithmically before any write into someone else's repository: a package that fails the check is copied nowhere, and no bypass flag exists.

p.STD-TERMS: Terms. The **standards package** is the directory `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/` in toolRoot. The **installed copy** is the same directory relative to patchesDir. The **managed manifest block** is the lines of the product `vibe.toml` between the markers `# codkit:begin standards` and `# codkit:end standards`. A **carrier** is where a file's licence information lives: a header comment in the file itself or an adjacent sidecar `<file name>.license`. The **licence policy** is `toolRoot/config/license-policy.json`. A **holder** is a string from the `holders` of the policy.

package.title: 1. The standards package

facts.STD-PACKAGE-LOCATION: The only source of the package is `toolRoot/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/`; exactly one `v*` directory exists at that location, otherwise the Codkit installation is corrupted (`CK-E-INTERNAL`). The version is read from `[package] version` of the package `vibe.toml` with the regular expression `^version = "([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)"$` and must match the directory name without the `v`.
facts.STD-SHIPPED-PACKAGES: **Shipped packages (development version 1.0.0).** Every package of the set carries 1.0.0 and is changed in place under that number (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0` in the conventions, `DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION` below). The tool ships a **set** of vibe packages under `toolRoot/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/<name>/v<version>/`; every name has exactly one `v*` directory, otherwise `CK-E-INTERNAL`. The **universal** set, delivered to every patch set whatever it forks: `standards` (mandatory, the edition of the norms) and `agent-skills` (the agent skills, §1a). Beside them the installation carries the packages of the project types (`STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`). `codkit standards load` delivers **every** package this patch set is due in one run; `standards check` checks them all; the components block of the notice lists them all (`STD-NOTICE-COMPONENTS-BLOCK` already walks `org.vibevm.codkit/*`). Decision D-S3-1 of campaign CODKIT-STANDARDS-03: one delivery instead of a second command; a separate package instead of skills inside the standard, because the version of a norm must not change when a harness procedure is edited.
facts.STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE: **The packages of a project type.** A norm is universal; a seam is a fact about one family of upstreams. So the shipped set has two halves: the universal one above, and the packages a project type names in its `standards` area (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-STANDARDS`), which sit under the same group directory and are delivered **only** to a patch set that declares that type. Edition 1.0.0 of the split: the seam catalogue left the `standards` package and became `org.vibevm.codkit/seams-vscode`, the package of the `vscode` type, with its own `vibe.toml`, README, licence carriers, REUSE registry and boot snippet `boot/77-flow-codkit-seams-vscode.xml`; the `generic` type names no package and is delivered the universal two. The engine never infers a type package from a directory listing: the type names its packages, a directory nobody named reaches nobody, and a name the installation cannot answer is `CK-E-INTERNAL` (a damaged installation), never a short delivery. `codkit standards load` and `codkit standards check` therefore read `codkit.json` for the type and refuse without one (`STD-LOAD-ROOTS`); the manifest block, the components block of the notice and every summary treat a type package exactly like a universal one.
facts.STD-PACKAGE-IDENTITY: The package identity is `(group, name, version)` = `(org.vibevm.codkit, standards, <version>)`; the manifest `vibe.toml` carries `kind = "flow"`, `license = "UPL-1.0"` and a `[boot_snippet]` with `category = "flow"`. The content of an edition under a released version never changes; a change to a standard is a new version.
facts.STD-PACKAGE-REQUIRED-FILES: The mandatory files of the package: `vibe.toml`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` (without an extension — licence detectors compare its text with the canonical one), `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` for every licence used in a carrier, `REUSE.toml`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (only when there are third-party files), the boot snippet named by `[boot_snippet] source`, and at least one document under `vibevm/vibespecs/flows/standards/`. Edition 1.0.0 of the `standards` package: `STANDARDS-PROTOCOL.xml`, `minimal-intervention.xml`, the boot snippet `boot/75-flow-codkit-standards.xml`, the pilot assets of `STD-PACKAGE-PILOT-ASSETS` (`seam-catalogue.xml` was a third document of the edition until it moved into the package of the project type, `STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`). The same mandatory files hold for a type package, which has no assets and therefore no `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`.
facts.STD-PACKAGE-SHIPS-IN-THE-TARBALL: The directory `vibevm/vibepacks` is part of `files` in `package.json` and of the npm artifact; the test `packageManifest.test.ts` requires `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v1.0.0/LICENSE` in the list of packed files, and the tarball bounds are owned by PROP-002 `TOOL-PACKAGE-TAR-BOUND` — the campaign does not choose them; by owner ruling of 2026-09-07 `unpackedSize` was raised to 50_000_000, because the ratchet fired on planned work (the numbers are in that anchor).
facts.STD-PACKAGE-LANGUAGE: The prose of the standards, the boot snippet and the package README are English (owner decision of 2026-09-06, `DECISION-STD-LANGUAGE`); the licence notice in every carrier, in `LICENSE` and in the README is given twice — in English and in Russian (`LIC-NOTICE-BILINGUAL`); the UPL text is English only. Identifiers, anchors and paths are English. The specifications of Codkit itself are Russian today and are being translated into English in full by separate work (DEF in the campaign plan); the language of a product's specifications is the product's own business.
facts.STD-TOOL-LICENCE-IS-UPL: Codkit as a whole is released under UPL-1.0 (owner decision of 2026-09-06, verbatim: «Поменять лицензию Codkit на UPL»): the root `LICENSE.md` (the notice in English and in Russian, then the UPL text, then a paragraph about third-party dependencies), `package.json` `license = "UPL-1.0"`, the root entry of `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, the anchor in `common/PROP-000` (the tombstone `LICENSE-PROPRIETARY`, the new `LICENSE-UPL`) and the risk row `CK-R-LEGAL-001` change in one commit (the `licensing` flow: every licence statement together). The standards package carries the same licence as the tool, so the root notice has no exceptions.
facts.STD-LICENCE-SCOPES: Three licence scopes, and none of them replaces another: (1) the **package** — the `LICENSE` and `REUSE.toml` inside the package directory describe the package only and travel with it as part of the byte-for-byte copy; (2) the **product repository** — Codkit never reads, copies or changes its root licence file, and it never leaves the product repository; (3) the **fork tree** — the licence files and notices of the fork and the licence fields of `product.json` are upstream files, and changing them is an ordinary delta artifact authored in the patch set (a config-overlay for the `product.json` fields, a resource-file or an add-file patch for the texts), never a side effect of `standards load` or `codkit load`. `REUSE.toml` obeys the same rule.
facts.STD-PACKAGE-IS-VIBE-CHECKED: The package specifications obey the vibe dialect: `vibe check` in the Codkit repository scans `vibevm/vibepacks/**/*.xml` and `*.md` and must stay at zero errors; the same package, consumed by a scratch project through `vibe install --offline`, gives a clean `vibe check` and a snippet in `STATIC`.

p.std-package-tree-sample: The package tree, drawn when the edition was numbered 0.1.0 and unchanged in shape since (every file on the left carries a carrier, except those listed in `LIC-UNSCANNED-SET`; edition 1.0.0 added `vibevm/vibespecs/flows/standards/seam-catalogue.xml` at the end and then gave it away to the package of the project type, `STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`):

package.fence: vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v1.0.0/ vibe.toml # header `#` README.md # header <!-- --> LICENSE # not scanned: 3 header lines + the UPL text LICENSES/UPL-1.0.txt # not scanned: the SPDX text verbatim LICENSES/MIT.txt # not scanned: the SPDX text verbatim (a third-party file) REUSE.toml # not scanned: the registry of third-party files THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md # header <!-- -->; generated by `license notices` assets/codkit.svg # the logo: header after <?xml?> assets/codkit-mark.svg # the mark without a background: header assets/codkit.png # raster 512: an own binary file, sidecar assets/codkit.png.license assets/codkit-128.png # raster 128: sidecar assets/codkit-128.png.license assets/third-party/feather/package.svg # third-party (MIT): sidecar + an annotation in REUSE.toml assets/third-party/feather/package.svg.license vibevm/vibespecs/boot/75-flow-codkit-standards.xml # header after <?xml?> vibevm/vibespecs/flows/standards/STANDARDS-PROTOCOL.xml vibevm/vibespecs/flows/standards/minimal-intervention.xml

p.STD-PACKAGE-PILOT-ASSETS: A pilot of the licence machinery on real bytes and at the same time the **Codkit logo** (owner decision of 2026-09-06: «сгенерить какую-нибудь иконку для codkit и запилотировать на ней»; «это будет логотип нашего продукта»). The mark is a delta inside marker brackets: two bracket strokes `[ ]` (the marker blocks `codkit:begin`/`codkit:end`, amber) and a triangle Δ between them (the delta over the fork itself, light blue on a dark blue gradient). The files: `assets/codkit.svg` — the icon with a background (sha256 `80e1120ffe4d0748bf9c440a67c48ed31c7d22665e0b062404502e1268545d49`), `assets/codkit-mark.svg` — the mark without a background, for light backgrounds (`d2118a56a9ad1d23ec2658b2edb7a759ca6a23aa4ed440253de1b2490eecbd2b`), `assets/codkit.png` — a 512×512 raster (`8990e15afc5ca5ae353f365be17138c7d7560ac5c08fc3d97d442fdb6878cae4`), `assets/codkit-128.png` (`668bef6c28ce92342cff922372d5185ff2165b9efb35036f086e6d762fd2fb4d`); both PNGs are own binary files with a sidecar; the SVGs carry a header. All four are produced from one geometry by the script `tools/make-logo.py` (Pillow, 4× supersampling, LANCZOS) and are reproduced by it byte for byte; the logo is the committed bytes, the script is for redrawing. The third-party pilot asset is `assets/third-party/feather/package.svg`: the `package` icon of the Feather Icons set at tag `v4.29.1` (MIT, Cole Bemis; sha256 `d6fef5e22b890eb614ebbe336491012f726f34e78ca3a90a436c238d1ac104e0`; a sidecar with the holder of the original source, an annotation in `REUSE.toml`, a row in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, `LICENSES/MIT.txt` — the SPDX text verbatim, sha256 `b05785f9f18e6716bab63424b11454513b9943a222595b70411009202fc592b5`). The package README shows the mark and names the third-party file as a working example.

facts.STD-SKILLS-PACKAGE-IDENTITY: The identity is `(org.vibevm.codkit, agent-skills, <version>)`; the manifest `vibe.toml`: `kind = "flow"`, `license = "UPL-1.0"`, a minimal `[boot_snippet]` (two lines: the skills are projected, they route and restate nothing — the projection of skills is not a boot snippet by itself, PROP-018 §2.5 of VibeVM, but a `flow` package carries a snippet by its form), and `[[skill]]` sections, one per skill. The mandatory files are those of the standards package (`STD-PACKAGE-REQUIRED-FILES`) without the assets; every carrier bears the notice; the scope of the notice `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` covers the package through the path `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/**` with no edit.
facts.STD-SKILLS-DECLARATION: The declaration form is VibeVM's `SKILL-TABLE-SHAPE`: `[[skill]] name = "<name>"` (the directory name in the harness), `path = "vibevm/vibespecs/skills/<name>"` (a directory with `SKILL.md` and nested `scripts/`, `agents/`; the path is written explicitly — the package manager does not resolve the `spec/` alias during projection, checked 2026-09-07), `description` (mandatory for us: the lazy-push trigger, one sentence in English), and `agents` is not set (every harness). A skill body addresses its own scripts by the projection path (`.<agent>/skills/<name>/scripts/…`), not by `<codkit-tool-root>`.
facts.STD-SKILLS-ROSTER-0-1-0: A tombstone (owner ruling of 2026-09-08, `DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0`): the roster it carried is `STD-SKILLS-ROSTER-1-0-0` below, with the same four skills - the package moved from 0.1.0 to the development version 1.0.0 and its directory moved with it. The anchor is neither renamed nor deleted (`NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR`).
facts.STD-SKILLS-ROSTER-1-0-0: The roster of 1.0.0: `ck-resolve` — resolving a cycle blocker by an explicit assignment (moved from `packages/codkit/claude/skills/ck-resolve/` with no change of meaning); `ck-orient` — orientation by reading only (`where`, `status`, `verify`, the inventory), with a state report and no edits; `ck-intervene` — the router for the choice of an intervention layer: the decision tree of human protocol 03 and the "area → owning specification" table from the README of the product's own catalogue (`MI-OWN-README-ROUTES-TO-THE-OWNING-SPEC`); `ck-review-intervention` — the reviewer's checklist over the `CONF-*` of the standard, with the output "artifact → norm → done/not done/where".
facts.STD-SKILLS-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH: The only source of the skills is the package: the directory `packages/codkit/claude/skills/` is removed from the repository; the profile `packages/codkit/claude/` keeps only what VibeVM does not project (`settings.json` with the hook and the deny profile, `rules/`, `agents/`, the managed blocks of `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`); `settings.json` refers to the skill scripts by the projection path. Installing the profile into a product: `codkit standards load` → `vibe install --offline` → `vibe skill install` → copying the Claude-specific parts by the agent protocol; `agentProtocol.test.ts` and the `check.mjs` of the agent protocol check the new location. Decision D-S3-2.
facts.STD-SKILLS-LANGUAGE: Skill bodies are in English, with no product names; the tool is mentioned operationally (commands, exit codes); every skill names its stop conditions and what it does not do (commits, editing the fork tree by hand, widening the packet).

licensing.title: 2. The licence markup of the package

p.LIC-POLICY-FILE: The policy is `toolRoot/config/license-policy.json`, strict schema `{"codkitLicensePolicy":1,"holders":[<string>+],"ownLicense":"UPL-1.0","allowedThirdParty":[<SPDX-id>*],"allowedExceptions":[<SPDX-exception-id>*]}` (Zod, an unknown field is an error); it is read only from toolRoot through the contained reader (PROP-002 `CONTAINED-FILE-IO`) and is never shadowed by a file of the patch set (the same rule as `CONVENTIONS-SINGLE-DEFINITION`). The lists are edited by a human; widening the allowlist is a separate deliberate decision, not a side effect.

p.LIC-SPDX-ID-LIST: The list of SPDX identifiers is the data file `toolRoot/config/spdx-license-ids.json`: `{"codkitSpdxLicenseIds":1,"listVersion":"…","releaseDate":"…","ids":[…]}`, 739 identifiers of the SPDX list of 2026-09-03 (version `01b8052`), with the sidecar `spdx-license-ids.json.license` (`CC0-1.0`, source `json/licenses.json` of the `spdx/license-list-data` repository). An update is a regeneration from the same SPDX file by the same command as recorded in the campaign plan; the list is not edited by hand. An identifier is valid when it is in the list; the form `LicenseRef-*` is recognized syntactically and is forbidden in the package; `NOASSERTION` is forbidden.

facts.LIC-CARRIER-HEADER: A text file carries a header in its first **20 non-empty lines**: at least one copyright line and exactly one `SPDX-License-Identifier` line. The header stands right after the prelude of the file (`<?xml …?>`, a shebang, a Python encoding line, `<!DOCTYPE>`, YAML front matter), wrapped in the comment of the file's language; the check does not look at the comment markers.
facts.LIC-HEADER-BLOCK-ENDS-AT-SPDX: The carrier block ends at the `SPDX-License-Identifier` line: copyright lines are read only from the lines of the window up to and including it; everything below is file content, even when it looks like a copyright. The reason: the table header `| Path | Copyright | License | Source |` of the notices file matches the regular expression of a copyright line and without this rule would make an own file "third-party" (found by the reference run of 2026-09-06, `DECISION-LIC-HEADER-BLOCK`).
facts.LIC-CARRIER-SIDECAR: A file that cannot carry a comment (JSON, CSV, `lock` files, a binary file — a file with a zero byte in its first 8 KiB, a file that is not UTF-8) carries a sidecar `<file name>.license` with the same lines without comment markers; when a sidecar is present the content of the file itself is not scanned. A file and its sidecar are an inseparable pair: they are copied, renamed and deleted together; a sidecar without its file is an error (`orphan sidecar`), and a binary file without a sidecar and without an annotation is an error. Metadata inside a binary (PNG `tEXt`, XMP, VERSIONINFO) is not a carrier and is not read.
facts.LIC-CARRIER-PRECEDENCE: The source of a file's licence information is chosen in the REUSE order: (1) the sidecar; (2) a `REUSE.toml` annotation with `precedence = "override"`; (3) the header in the file (the window of 20 non-empty lines); (4) an annotation with `precedence = "closest"` (the default) or `"aggregate"`. A file with none of the four is the error `no licence carrier`. Edition 3 (2026-09-07): an annotation is a carrier in its own right for a file whose extension has no comment style in `LIC-COMMENT-STYLES` (`LIC-CARRIER-ANNOTATION`); for an extension that has a comment style the header stays mandatory, and an annotation does not replace it. Under `closest`/`aggregate` a disagreement between the header (or the sidecar) and the annotation is the error `carrier disagrees with annotation`.
facts.LIC-CARRIER-ANNOTATION: A file with no comment style (an image, a font, JSON, CSV, a binary file) counts as covered when an `[[annotations]]` annotation of a `REUSE.toml` registry (a nested one included, `LIC-REGISTRY-NESTED`) applies to it: a `.license` sidecar stays allowed for such files, but is not the only carrier. This is how a directory of hundreds of images is covered by one annotation over a mask instead of a hundred sidecars (owner decision of 2026-09-07). A file with a comment style, without a header and without a sidecar, is a `LICENSE-HEADER` error even when an annotation covers it: a source file must stay self-sufficient when a single file is copied.
facts.LIC-REGISTRY-NESTED: `license check` reads a `REUSE.toml` in **every** directory of the tree being checked (REUSE 3.3 allows a registry in a subdirectory); annotation paths are relative to the directory of their own registry. A file matched by annotations from several registries is assigned the annotation from the deepest directory, and at equal depth the first one in file order. This lets the own directory of a fork, whose root belongs to upstream, carry a registry of its own.
facts.LIC-ANNOTATION-OWN: An annotation whose `SPDX-FileComment` does not begin with `third-party;` is an **own** annotation: its `SPDX-FileCopyrightText` must name a holder from the `holders` of the policy, and its `SPDX-License-Identifier` must equal `ownLicense`; otherwise every covered file gets a `LICENSE-HEADER` error with the text `own annotation names a foreign holder or licence`. Third-party annotations follow `LIC-THIRD-PARTY-REGISTRY` unchanged. `SPDX-FileComment` is not mandatory on an own annotation.
facts.LIC-HEADER-WINDOW: The search window is the first 20 non-empty lines; a header below the window does not count (`CRITICAL-CONSTRAINTS-LIVE-AT-THE-START-OR-END`).
facts.LIC-UNSCANNED-SET: Not marked up and not scanned: `LICENSE`, `COPYING*`, everything under `LICENSES/`, every `*.license`, `REUSE.toml`, the `.git` directory. A symbolic link anywhere in the package is a package error (`LICENSE-PACKAGE`). This is the same set that `reuse lint` ignores.
facts.LIC-COPYRIGHT-REGEX: A copyright line (modelled on reuse-tool; comment markers at the edges are allowed): `(SPDX-FileCopyrightText:\s*)?(Copyright\s*(\(c\)|©)?|©)\s*(?<years>\d{4}(\s*[-,]\s*\d{4})*)?\s+(?<holder>.+?)\s*$` with the `u` flag; `holder` is stripped of trailing comment markers (`-->`, `*/`, `-*)`) and spaces. The year is the year the file was created (a range is allowed, it is not updated annually). A line of the form `Modifications Copyright (c) <year> <holder>` marks our own edits to a third-party file: it takes no part in the classification of the file.
facts.LIC-SPDX-REGEX: The licence line: `SPDX-License-Identifier:\s*(?<expr>[A-Za-z0-9.+\-]+(\s+(AND|OR|WITH)\s+[A-Za-z0-9.+\-]+)*)`; the expression is split into identifiers by `AND`/`OR`/`WITH`; every identifier must be in the SPDX list (`LIC-SPDX-ID-LIST`), otherwise an error with the text `not an SPDX identifier: …` (for `UPL`, `UPL 1.0`, `UPL1.0`, `upl-1.0` the text `the only valid form is UPL-1.0` is added). Two `SPDX-License-Identifier` lines in the window are an error.
facts.LIC-FILE-CLASSIFICATION: By the copyright lines of the block (without the `Modifications Copyright` lines): every holder from `holders` → an **own file**: a year is mandatory on every line and the expression must be exactly `ownLicense`. At least one holder outside `holders` → a **third-party file**: it must fall under a registry annotation (`LIC-THIRD-PARTY-REGISTRY`), otherwise the error `holder not in policy and no REUSE.toml annotation covers the file (typo in the holder, or an undeclared third-party file)`; the licence of the annotation must agree with the expression of the carrier; every identifier of the expression must be in `allowedThirdParty` (the exceptions after `WITH` — in `allowedExceptions`); `LicenseRef-*` and `NOASSERTION` are an error, "even when the file has a banner". Our copyright is never put on a third-party file; other parties' notices are never removed.
facts.LIC-NOT-A-TEMPLATE-MATCH: The check does **not** compare the header with a reference string as a whole: the year, the case of the markers, the spaces, the order of the lines, extra copyright lines and link lines all vary legitimately and do not affect the verdict.
facts.LIC-NOTICE-BILINGUAL: The licence notice in the carrier of an own file is four lines: the copyright line, the English link to the UPL, the Russian link to the UPL, the `SPDX-License-Identifier` line (owner decision of 2026-09-06). The check requires only the first and the fourth, while the shipped package must carry all four in every own carrier and in `LICENSE` — `shippedStandards.test.ts` asserts this by substrings of both links; the Russian line is a notice, and where the two diverge the English text governs.
facts.LIC-THIRD-PARTY-REGISTRY: The registry of third-party files is the package `REUSE.toml` (`version = 1`, optionally `SPDX-PackageName`, `SPDX-PackageSupplier`, `SPDX-PackageDownloadLocation`): every third-party file, besides its own carrier (the original header or a sidecar), falls under an `[[annotations]]` entry with `path` (a string or an array of REUSE globs: `*`, `**`), `precedence` (`closest` by default | `aggregate` | `override`), `SPDX-FileCopyrightText`, `SPDX-License-Identifier` and a mandatory `SPDX-FileComment` of the form `third-party; <URL, version/tag, sha256 for binaries>`. The annotation is the only source from which `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` is generated; an unknown key, `version ≠ 1`, an annotation without a copyright or without a licence — `LICENSE-PACKAGE`. Annotations may cover own files as well (REUSE semantics), but the shipped package does not use that: every scanned file of it resolves through a header or a sidecar (asserted by `shippedStandards.test.ts`) — the mandate "every file carries licence information".
facts.LIC-MANIFEST-FIELD: The package `vibe.toml` must contain the line `license = "UPL-1.0"` (regular expression `^license = "(.*)"$`, the value equal to `ownLicense`); otherwise `LICENSE-PACKAGE`.
facts.LIC-LICENSE-FILE-SHAPE: `LICENSE`: the header is every line up to the first empty line, no fewer than two: line 1 is a copyright line with a holder from the policy, the rest are the English and the Russian links to the UPL; then an empty line; then the body — the text of UPL 1.0, equal to `LICENSES/UPL-1.0.txt` from its third line on (the first line of the SPDX file is a placeholder, the second is empty), compared by `LIC-TEXT-NORMALIZATION`.
facts.LIC-LICENSES-DIR: `LICENSES/` contains exactly one `<SPDX-ID>.txt` file per identifier that occurs in the carriers of the package (the own licence and the licences of third-party files; `WITH` exceptions need no texts), and nothing beyond that: a missing text and an extra text are both `LICENSE-PACKAGE`. The text of `UPL-1.0.txt` is compared with the canonical one (`LIC-CANONICAL-TEXT-EMBEDDED`); the texts of other licences are taken verbatim from SPDX (`text/<ID>.txt`), and the check requires them to be present and non-empty — Codkit does not embed the canonical texts of other parties' licences (`LIC-OTHER-TEXTS-PRESENCE-ONLY`).
facts.LIC-OTHER-TEXTS-PRESENCE-ONLY: For licences other than the own one, the presence and non-emptiness of `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` is checked, not its verbatimness: embedding the texts of every allowed licence into Codkit would be data nobody verifies; the verbatimness of another party's text is confirmed by `reuse download <ID>` when the file is added (`LIC-CHECK-CALLSITES`).
facts.LIC-CANONICAL-TEXT-EMBEDDED: The canonical text of UPL-1.0 — the file `text/UPL-1.0.txt` of the SPDX licence list (1837 bytes, sha256 `2f81e75033a0c872ab9725b36081e363f0c9e6c45585c35930edb66043fdc576`) — is embedded verbatim in `packages/codkit/src/lib/licenseTexts.ts` as a string constant; this is the only oracle for "the licence text has not been changed" (the acceptance "a LICENSE with a changed word → 1").
facts.LIC-TEXT-NORMALIZATION: Normalization before licence texts are compared: the quotation marks `“ ” „ "` and `‘ ’ '` are folded to the ASCII `"` and `'`; any run of whitespace (line breaks included) becomes one space; leading and trailing spaces are dropped. The reason: the SPDX text carries typographic quotation marks in one place (`“Larger Work”`), while the line wrapping in `LICENSE` is editorial; the SPDX matching rules count such variants as equivalent.
facts.LIC-NOTICES-FILE: `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` is generated by `codkit license notices` from the registry annotations whose holder is outside `holders`, in exactly this shape: the four-line notice header of the package in `<!-- -->`, the heading `# Third-party notices`, the paragraph `This package includes the following third-party components. Each keeps its own copyright notice and license; the license texts are in \`LICENSES/\`.` and the table `| Path | Copyright | License | Source |` with one row per annotation (`Path` — the annotation paths in backticks, comma-separated; `Source` — the `SPDX-FileComment` without the `third-party; ` prefix), the rows in the order of the annotations in the file. The file is not edited by hand: a divergence from the generated one is `LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY` ("stale"), its absence with a non-empty registry is `LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY`, and its presence with an empty registry is `LICENSE-PACKAGE`.

p.lic-header-templates-lead: The header templates are four lines, unchanged in substance for every own file (only the year and the comment markers vary). What each is for: the first is the notice of copyright (the word `Copyright`, the year, the name — the form accepted both by 17 U.S.C. §401 and by Art. 1271 of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation); the second is the "reference to the UPL", the minimal condition of the UPL itself in the wording Oracle uses; the third is the same reference in Russian (`LIC-NOTICE-BILINGUAL`); the fourth is the only thing scanners and SBOM tools understand. `All rights reserved` is not written.

p.LIC-COMMENT-STYLES: Comment styles by extension for `license annotate` (a minimal set, extended only by editing this table and the code together): `#` — toml, yaml, yml, py, sh, bash, zsh, Dockerfile, Makefile, gitignore, gitattributes, editorconfig, properties, ini, conf, rb, pl, r, ps1; `//` — java, kt, kts, go, js, mjs, cjs, ts, tsx, jsx, c, h, cpp, hpp, cs, rs, swift, dart, scala, groovy, gradle, proto; `/* … */` — css, scss, less; `<!-- … -->` — md, html, htm, xml, xsl, xsd, svg, xhtml, vue; `--` — sql, lua, hs; `;` — clj, cljs, edn, lisp, el; `%` — tex, sty; `REM` — bat, cmd. facts.LIC-NEVER-MODIFY-THE-UPL-TEXT: Never change the UPL text and never start a `LICENSE-ADDONS` with "corrections": a changed UPL is no longer the UPL. Additional permissions, should they be needed, go into a separate file that only widens the rights; other conditions mean a licence of our own, `LicenseRef-*`, named honestly.
facts.LIC-NEVER-CLAIM-A-THIRD-PARTY-FILE: Never put our copyright on a third-party file and never remove other parties' notices; our substantial edits go on a separate line `Modifications Copyright (c) <year> <holder>`, and the licence of the file stays the original one.
facts.LIC-NEVER-WRITE-ALL-RIGHTS-RESERVED: Never write `All rights reserved` in the headers of the package.
facts.LIC-NEVER-BYPASS: Never give `standards load` a flag that bypasses the check; the only way to "allow" a file is to mark it up and declare it by the rules, that is, to take responsibility for it.
facts.LIC-NEVER-REWRITE-THROUGH-A-PARSER: Never rewrite a file of the package through a parser that loses comments: a copy is byte for byte; `annotate --third-party` **appends** an `[[annotations]]` entry at the end of `REUSE.toml` instead of reserializing it.
facts.LIC-NEVER-EDIT-NOTICES-BY-HAND: Never edit `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` by hand — only `codkit license notices`.
facts.LIC-NEVER-CREATE-LRGRWRKS: Never create `lrgrwrks.txt` — the Larger Works mechanism of the UPL needs a separate owner decision.

check.title: 3. The check: the `license check` algorithm; the `annotate` and `notices` commands

p.LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM: The input is a package directory (by default the standards package in toolRoot). The steps: (1) load the policy and the SPDX list; (2) walk the directory recursively, with the paths sorted lexicographically by UTF-8 in POSIX form, excluding `.git`; a symbolic link is a `LICENSE-PACKAGE` error and the enumeration continues (every error, not the first); (3) read every `REUSE.toml` of the tree (`LIC-THIRD-PARTY-REGISTRY`, `LIC-REGISTRY-NESTED`; a parse error is `LICENSE-PACKAGE`); (4) exclude `LIC-UNSCANNED-SET`; (5) for every file choose the carrier by `LIC-CARRIER-PRECEDENCE`, taking `LIC-CARRIER-ANNOTATION` into account: binariness is a zero byte in the first 8 KiB; a file that cannot be decoded, or a file without a comment style that has neither a sidecar nor an annotation, is an error; (6) extract the copyright lines from the block (`LIC-HEADER-BLOCK-ENDS-AT-SPDX`) and the SPDX line of the carrier (for an annotation — its fields); the errors: no copyright line; two SPDX lines; an invalid identifier; (7) classify the file (`LIC-FILE-CLASSIFICATION`, `LIC-ANNOTATION-OWN`): own — a year and exactly `ownLicense`; third-party — an annotation, agreement of the licences, the allowlist, the ban on `LicenseRef-*`/`NOASSERTION`; (8) orphan sidecars: every `*.license` must have an owning file; (9) consistency of the package: `LIC-MANIFEST-FIELD`, `LIC-LICENSE-FILE-SHAPE`, `LIC-LICENSES-DIR`, `LIC-NOTICES-FILE`; (9a) for a directory that is not a vibe package (the runtime library, PROP-015 `RT-EVERY-FILE-CARRIES-THE-BANNER`) the call passes `packageShape: false`: step (9) and the notices check are skipped, and the file carriers are checked as usual; (10) the report `LIC-CHECK-REPORT` — every row of `checked[]` has a `carrier` field (`header` | `sidecar` | `annotation`) and the registry path for an annotation. The check writes nothing and runs no git.

p.LIC-CHECK-REPORT: Every problem is a separate line `error CK-E-LICENSE-HEADER: <path>: <reason>` (the carrier of a file), `error CK-E-LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY: <path>: <reason>` (a third-party file: undeclared, a licence outside the allowlist, a divergence from the annotation, `LicenseRef`/`NOASSERTION`; the notices absent or stale) or `error CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE: <path>: <reason>` (the package level) with a `hint`, then the total `N files checked, M problems`; under `--json` — `data: {dir, files, checked: [{path, carrier: "header"|"sidecar"|"annotation", kind: "own"|"third-party", license}], problems: [{code, file, message}], licences: {own: […], thirdParty: […]}, policy: {holders, ownLicense, allowedThirdParty}}`; the paths are relative to the package directory, with the POSIX separator.

p.LIC-CHECK-EXIT-CODES: The codes: 0 — clean; 1 — there are problems; 2 — a startup error (the directory does not exist or is not a directory, the policy or the SPDX list is broken, a file is unreadable by permissions).

p.LIC-CHECK-CALLSITES: The call sites: (1) the unit test `shippedStandards.test.ts` in `npm run floor` — the check of the shipped package, red on any problem (this is the CI of the package repository); (2) `codkit standards load` — the first action, before any write; (3) `codkit standards check` — on the installed copy; (4) a manual `codkit license check [<dir>]`. `reuse lint` (the pip package `reuse`) is an optional manual cross-check: on a clean package it must give a clean verdict, and `reuse download <ID>` is the source of the verbatim texts of other parties' licences; there is no runtime dependency on Python.

p.LIC-REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTATION: The reference implementation of the algorithm is `tools/license-reference.py` (Python ≥ 3.11, `tomllib`) with the fixture oracle `tools/license-fixtures.py` (the cases S29 (a)–(s), one defect each on copies of a package of the same layout — synthetic in the tests, the shipped one in acceptance); the TypeScript implementation must give the same codes on the same fixtures — this is asserted by the differential test `licenseReference.test.ts`, which is skipped with an explicit reason when `python3` ≥ 3.11 is unavailable and never counts as passed when skipped. The reference run of 2026-09-06 on the shipped package: 11 files checked, 0 problems; 20 cases of the oracle (the clean package and 19 defects) — all with the expected verdict.

p.LIC-ANNOTATE: `codkit license annotate [--dir <package>] <paths…> [--dry-run] [--year <YYYY>] [--holder <name>]` gives an own file its carrier: a header in the comment style of its extension (`LIC-COMMENT-STYLES`), inserted right after the prelude, or a sidecar for binary and comment-less formats; four lines from the templates (the year — `--year`, the current one by default; the holder — `--holder`, the first of `holders` by default, and it must be in the policy). It is idempotent: a file whose carrier already resolves is `unchanged`, and a repeat run changes nothing (`git diff` is empty). A third-party file (`--third-party --holder <holder> --license <SPDX-ID> --source <text>`): a sidecar or a header with the other party's holder and licence (without our lines), the licence must be on the allowlist and in the SPDX list, and an `[[annotations]]` entry is appended at the end of `REUSE.toml` with `path` = the exact path, `precedence = "closest"`, `SPDX-FileCopyrightText`, `SPDX-License-Identifier`, `SPDX-FileComment = "third-party; <source>"` (a `REUSE.toml` that has no `version = 1` is created); the command does not download `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` — it prints the hint `reuse download <ID>` or manual copying of the verbatim SPDX text. The paths are inside `--dir` (default `.`), otherwise `CK-E-CONFIG`. `--dry-run` prints the plan without writing. The codes: 0; 1 (a file outside the directory, an unknown licence, a holder outside the policy without `--third-party`); 2 (the environment).

p.LIC-NOTICES: `codkit license notices [--dir <package>] [--dry-run]` generates `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` by `LIC-NOTICES-FILE` from the registry: with a non-empty registry it writes the file atomically (a byte-identical one is not rewritten, and `unchanged` is printed); with an empty registry the file is not created, and an existing one is deleted with a line printed (it is a generated artifact). `--dry-run` prints the result to stdout without writing. The codes: 0; 1 (`REUSE.toml` does not parse); 2 (the environment).

manifest.title: 4. The managed block of the product manifest

p.STD-MANIFEST-BLOCK-FORM: The canonical block is exactly these bytes (the version is substituted; the line breaks are LF):

manifest.fence: # codkit:begin standards # Managed by `codkit standards load`; do not edit inside this block. [requires.packages."org.vibevm.codkit/standards"] version = "=1.0.0" link = "static" # codkit:end standards

facts.STD-MANIFEST-NO-TOML-PARSER: Codkit does not parse and does not reserialize the product `vibe.toml`: the block is found by a deterministic byte scan over whole marker lines (`# codkit:begin standards` / `# codkit:end standards`, with no trailing spaces), and everything outside the block belongs to someone else and is not touched by a single byte (`managed-blocks`: "Own exactly one delimited block; never touch a byte outside it"). A full table header `[requires.packages."org.vibevm.codkit/standards"]` inside the block is valid at any position in the file — checked with `tomllib` on two consumer manifests of different shapes: one ending with a `[requires.packages]` table and one ending with a `[[registry]]` element (`DECISION-STD-MANIFEST-BLOCK`).
facts.STD-MANIFEST-STATE-MACHINE: The states: **absent** — not a single marker → the block is appended at the end of the file: when the last byte is not LF, an LF is added, then an empty line, then the block with a trailing LF; **present** — exactly one begin, exactly one end, begin before end → the bytes from the start of the begin line to the end of the end line inclusive are compared with the canonical block: equal — the file is not rewritten; different — they are replaced atomically (`writeContainedFileAtomic`); **malformed** — any other combination (one marker, a repeat, end before begin) → `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 1, an exact report (the line numbers), nothing written; there is no auto-repair.
facts.STD-MANIFEST-ENTRY-OUTSIDE-BLOCK: A line containing `"org.vibevm.codkit/standards"` outside the block (a table of its own or an inline key in `[requires.packages]`) is `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 1, with the line number and the hint "remove your entry; the dependencies are kept by the codkit block": a second table with the same name would break the TOML, and an inline key would state the version twice.
facts.STD-MANIFEST-PRECONDITIONS: `vibe.toml` must exist in patchesDir as a regular file (the contained reader), be UTF-8 without CR (a CR is `CK-E-CRLF`, exit 1) and contain the line `[project]` — otherwise `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 2, hint "run vibe init in the patch set first; codkit does not create vibevm projects".
facts.STD-MANIFEST-TAIL-CAVEAT: The block opens a TOML table; keys a human appends after `# codkit:end standards` without a header `[…]` of their own land in the dependency table. `standards check` prints a warning (without a code) when there is a non-empty line that is not a comment between the end of the block and the next header; the product documentation (`13-standards.md`) names this rule.

notice.title: 4a. The file LICENSE-CODKIT.md

p.STD-NOTICE-FILE: Codkit ships the notice file `toolRoot/config/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (owner decisions of 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-07): a heading; two scope paragraphs — English and Russian — **by paths** (`STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS`); the managed components block (`STD-NOTICE-COMPONENTS-BLOCK`, empty in the shipped file); two paragraphs about the copies vibe builds (`STD-NOTICE-VIBE-COPIES`); the four notice lines (the copyright, the English and the Russian links; there is no SPDX line — the file is a notice, not a carrier for the check) and the text of UPL 1.0 (the body after the first empty line following the notice equals the canonical text by `LIC-TEXT-NORMALIZATION`; asserted by `shippedStandards.test.ts`). The file is part of `files` through `config`.

p.STD-NOTICE-TARGETS: The copies of the notice live in two roots of the product repository: `<patchesDir>/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` and `<patchesDir>/delta/own/codkit/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (the directories are created when absent; the path under the `codkit/` prefix — `DECISION-STD-NOTICE-UNDER-PREFIX`). Both delivering commands — `standards load` and `runtime load` (PROP-015 §4) — write each copy as a render of the template with the components block computed for this product (`STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-NOTICE`). The states of a copy are `absent` / `identical` (equal to the render) / `drift`; `drift` is `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` with the path and the hint `delete the copy and run codkit standards load`; `--dry-run` shows both copies in the plan; `standards check` and `runtime check` check both.

p.STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS: The scope of the notice is set **by paths**, not by listing the components in prose: everything Codkit delivers into a product lies only under the declared prefixes — `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/**` and its projection `vibevm/vibedeps/org.vibevm.codkit.*/**` (the packages), `delta/own/codkit/**` (the runtime library and the copy of the notice; `codkit load` materializes it into `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/**` of the fork tree), and the single file `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` in the product root. The paragraphs of the notice name these prefixes and say that outside them the notice licenses nothing, and that the lines in the marked managed blocks of the product files (`vibe.toml`, `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml`) are generated configuration, not licensed material. Three rules keep the claim by paths true, and `verify` checks them: Codkit writes only under the prefixes, the root notice and the marked blocks; the product does not place its own files under the prefixes (PROP-005 `OWN-CODKIT-PREFIX-RESERVED`); what is installed changes only as a whole, by version. The licence carriers in the files (headers, sidecars, annotations) remain: the path says what here belongs to Codkit, the carrier makes a single file self-sufficient.

p.STD-NOTICE-COMPONENTS-BLOCK: The notice carries a managed block between the lines `<!-- codkit:begin components -->` and `<!-- codkit:end components -->`; inside it there is one line per installed component: `<name> <version> <path>/` (for example `standards 1.0.0 vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v1.0.0/`, `runtime 1.0.0 delta/own/codkit/`), sorted by name. The block is computed from what stands in the product: the directories `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/<name>/v*/` (every version present, each on its own line) and the version literal of `delta/own/codkit/common/version.ts` (PROP-015 `RT-VERSION-LITERAL`). Both delivering commands rewrite the block every time; `check` compares the copy with a fresh render, so `standards check` and `runtime check` give one result. The shipped template carries an empty block.

p.STD-NOTICE-VIBE-COPIES: Separate paragraphs (EN and RU) permit explicitly: `vibe install` compiles the snippets of the package into the generated files of the boot lane (`vibevm/vibespecs/boot/STATIC.*`, `INDEX.md`), builds the projection of the package under `vibevm/vibedeps/` and may convert files (`README.md` → `README.xml`); these files are copies and derivative works of the package permitted by the licence; the reference to the UPL for them is vibe's provenance comment naming the package, together with the notice itself; the repository owner has no other obligation in connection with them. This is a statement of the holder that removes a doubt where the UPL permits anyway (owner decision of 2026-09-07).

p.STD-NOTICE-LEGACY-COPY: The copy at the legacy path of edition 2, `delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md`: both delivering commands remove it after writing the copy under the prefix and print `moved`; when it is present, `check` prints `legacy-copy` (a warning, not a finding); the name `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` stays in the set of files delivered by Codkit (PROP-005 `OWN-DELIVERED-BY-CODKIT`) so that the legacy copy does not give a false `OWN-UNCOVERED`.

p.STD-LICENSE-PRINTS-REUSE-ROWS: Besides the template and the recommendations, `codkit standards license` prints a ready `[[annotations]]` entry for the product's own `REUSE.toml`: `path` with the four paths of the scope (`LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/**`, `vibevm/vibedeps/org.vibevm.codkit.*/**`, `delta/own/codkit/**`), `precedence = "aggregate"`, `SPDX-FileCopyrightText` with the holder from the Codkit policy, `SPDX-License-Identifier = "UPL-1.0"`, `SPDX-FileComment = "third-party; delivered by Codkit, see LICENSE-CODKIT.md"`. The product adds the entry at its own wish (`REUSE-TOML-FOLLOWS-THE-SAME-RULE`); Codkit does not write the product's `REUSE.toml`. `--json`: `data.reuseAnnotation`.

p.STD-NOTICE-IS-A-DELIVERED-OWN-FILE: `delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` is a delivered own file: `load` copies it into `src/vs/<ownDirName>/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` of the tree, `save` mirrors it back, `ci` commits it into the own commit of its generated branch — like any own file (`isDeliveredOwnFile` does not change). Two exceptions: (1) unit coverage — the name `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` is in the "not own code" set of the manifest (`NOT_OWN_CODE` in `layers/ownManifest.ts`, next to `patchset.delta.json` and `.gitkeep`), and `verify` requires neither a unit nor a manifest entry for it (PROP-005 §3 `OWN-MANIFEST`, a refinement of campaign STANDARDS); (2) the release branch — `STD-NOTICE-RELEASE-EXCLUSION`. In everything else `verify`, `load`, `save` and `cycle` do not tell it apart.

p.STD-NOTICE-RELEASE-EXCLUSION: The release branch of the fork that `codkit publish` builds (PROP-007 §18 `PUBLISH-GENERATED-ORDER`, step (2) — the own commit) does **not** carry `src/vs/<ownDirName>/LICENSE-CODKIT.md`: the own snapshot of a publication is built by the predicate "a delivered own file, except `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`". Only `publish`: the generated `ci` branch (any profile), the cycle branch and the dev tree after `load` carry the file as usual — they are working trees, not a release. The predicate is one for the three functions of `generatedBranch.ts` (`assertGeneratedTargetOwnership`, `generatedHistoryFingerprint`, `appendGeneratedOwnCommit`) and is switched on by the option `omitLicenceNotice`, which `buildGeneratedTip` receives from `publish` and from nobody else; with the option on, the history fingerprint (`GENERATED-HISTORY-FINGERPRINT`) includes the marker `omit-licence-notice`, so that the `ci` tip and the `publish` tip never share a fingerprint. An own snapshot consisting of the notice alone is empty at publication — the own commit is skipped, the way any empty layer is skipped.

p.STD-NOTICE-LINKS-ARE-THE-PRODUCTS-CHOICE: The links to the file — from the product README, from a patch-set intervention in the fork's README — are placed by the product owner deliberately and at their own wish; Codkit does not edit a README. Codkit prints the text of the file and the recommendations: at install time (`STD-LOAD-NOTICE-PRINT`) and by `codkit standards license` (PROP-007 §24 `CMD-STANDARDS-LICENSE`); the rows of the scrape contract Codkit keeps in the product contract itself (`STD-SCRAPE-CONTRACT-ROWS`).

p.STD-SCRAPE-CONTRACT-ROWS: A clean export of the product repository is made by `vibe scrape` (PROP-056 of vibevm) by the product contract `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml`; so that the export does not carry the Codkit notice, the contract holds a `[[classify]]` row of kind delete with `patterns = ["LICENSE-CODKIT.md", "delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md", "delta/own/codkit/LICENSE-CODKIT.md"]` (the legacy path of edition 2 stays in the list — an export is cleaned of old copies as well), `owner = "vibe"` (the only owner value for delete in schema 1), `proof = "contract-assertion-v1"`, `modified = "delete"`, `require_match = false`, and an `[[assert]]` row of kind `paths-absent-v1` with the same paths. **Codkit keeps these rows in the product contract itself** — in the managed block `STD-SCRAPE-BLOCK-FORM` on every `standards load`, because a product may have a contract of its own and a human will forget the rows (owner decision of 2026-09-06, `DECISION-STD-SCRAPE-ROWS`). Codkit does not create a contract from scratch (the schema requires the product's health checks): when the file is absent — `STD-SCRAPE-NO-CONTRACT`. A contract at a non-standard path (`vibe scrape --contract`) is unknown to Codkit — for it the rows are printed by `codkit standards license`.

p.STD-SCRAPE-BLOCK-FORM: The canonical block in `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` is exactly these bytes (LF):

notice.fence:
# codkit:begin scrape # Managed by `codkit standards load`; do not edit inside this block. [[classify]] id = "remove-codkit-licence-notice" kind = "delete" patterns = ["LICENSE-CODKIT.md", "delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md"] owner = "vibe" proof = "contract-assertion-v1" modified = "delete" require_match = false
[[assert]] id = "codkit-licence-notice-absent" kind = "paths-absent-v1" patterns = ["LICENSE-CODKIT.md", "delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md"] # codkit:end scrape

p.STD-SCRAPE-STATE-MACHINE: The same state machine as the manifest block (`STD-MANIFEST-STATE-MACHINE`), with the markers `# codkit:begin scrape` / `# codkit:end scrape`: **absent** → the block is appended at the end of the file (LF normalization, an empty line, the block with a trailing LF — `[[classify]]` and `[[assert]]` elements at the end of the file after any table are valid, checked with `tomllib` and `vibe scrape contract check`, `STD-SCRAPE-VERIFIED`); **present** — equal to the canonical one → the file is not rewritten, different → the replacement happens only inside the block; **malformed** → `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 1, the line numbers, nothing written. A file with a CR is `CK-E-CRLF`. Both blocks — the manifest one and the contract one — are implemented by one module `managedBlock.ts` with parameters (the marker names, the canonical text, the "needles" for finding foreign entries).

p.STD-SCRAPE-ENTRY-OUTSIDE-BLOCK: A line outside the block that is not a comment (after trimming the spaces it does not begin with `#`) and contains any of the needles `remove-codkit-licence-notice`, `codkit-licence-notice-absent` or `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` is `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 1, with the line number and the hint "the scrape rows for the codkit licence notice are kept by codkit inside its block; remove your row": a second row with the same id breaks the schema (ids are unique), and a row of your own with the same path gives a conflict in the classification lattice (keep shadows delete) — Codkit does not parse the contract and does not guess which one would win.

p.STD-SCRAPE-NO-CONTRACT: The file `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` is absent → `standards load` writes nothing, prints `scrape contract: none - run vibe scrape contract init, then codkit standards load again to record the licence-notice rows` and continues (exit 0); `data.scrape.action = "no-contract"`. In this state `standards check` prints the same as information and does not change its exit code because of it: the absence of a contract is a state of the product, not a defect of the installation.

p.STD-SCRAPE-VERIFIED: Checked on 2026-09-06 (`vibe 1.0.0`, Linux): after `vibe scrape contract init` the block `STD-SCRAPE-BLOCK-FORM`, appended at the end of the contract (the file ends with a `[[healthcheck]]` element), parses with `tomllib` (the `classify` ids: `remove-vibevm`, `remove-vibe-state`, `remove-codkit-licence-notice`; the `assert` ids: `vibe-paths-absent`, `codkit-licence-notice-absent`), while `vibe scrape contract check` shows both copies of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` with the disposition `delete-unknown`, `rule_ids: ["remove-codkit-licence-notice"]`, and registers the assert; not one finding names our rows — the blockers belong to the default rows of the contract (`modified = "refuse"` on `vibe.toml` and on the contract itself), to the product's health check and to `scrape-platform-unsupported` (the mutation in epoch 1 is Windows only).

p.STD-LOAD-NOTICE-PRINT: At install time `standards load` prints, after the licence note, a block of recommendations (the heading `licence notice file:`; where the two copies live; that they are not edited; that the links to the file are the owner's choice, from the product README and from an intervention in the fork's README; that Codkit keeps the scrape contract rows in `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` itself, and what to do when there is no contract; that the full text of the file and the rows are printed by `codkit standards license`). The full text of the file is printed in the same run only when at least one copy was created; on `up to date` — the recommendations only. Under `--json` — `data.noticeFiles: [{path, action}]`, `data.recommendations: [...]`, and `data.noticeText` only on creation.

facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-SOURCE: Find the package (`STD-PACKAGE-LOCATION`); under the build condition `codkit-test` the variable `CODKIT_TEST_STANDARDS_SOURCE=<directory>` substitutes the location of the package (the test build only, modelled on `CODKIT_TEST_SAVE_REPLAY_CRASH_AT`).
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-LICENSE-GATE: Run `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` on the package; any problem → the full report, exit 1, **not one write** into patchesDir. This is the first action after the policy is read.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-MANIFEST-PRECHECK: Check `STD-MANIFEST-PRECONDITIONS`, classify the manifest block (`STD-MANIFEST-STATE-MACHINE`), check `STD-MANIFEST-ENTRY-OUTSIDE-BLOCK`; when `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` exists — classify the scrape block (`STD-SCRAPE-STATE-MACHINE`) and check `STD-SCRAPE-ENTRY-OUTSIDE-BLOCK`; a refusal comes before any write.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-TARGET-STATE: Classify the target `patchesDir/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/`: **absent**; **identical** — the same set of relative paths and the same bytes in every file (a symbolic link in the target is drift); **drift** — otherwise, with the list of `modified` / `extra` / `missing` paths. Classify both copies of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (`STD-NOTICE-TARGETS`) the same way: `absent` / `identical` / `drift`. The `.codkit-load-*` directories under `standards/` are unfinished Codkit runs: they are removed recursively before the classification, and each one is printed. Other `v*` directories are listed as `otherVersions` and are not touched.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-DRIFT-REFUSAL: **drift** of the package or of any `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copy → `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`, exit 1, the list of paths with their class, the hint "the installed standards package and the LICENSE-CODKIT.md copies are codkit-owned: move local edits into your own specs, delete <directory/file> and run codkit standards load again"; nothing is written and the manifest block is untouched.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-DRY-RUN: `--dry-run` gives the same plan (the files: create/unchanged; the manifest: append/update/unchanged; otherVersions; the `.codkit-load-*` to be removed) and the same exit code a real run would give, without a single write and without removing the temporary directories.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-FILES: **absent** → create the temporary directory `patchesDir/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/.codkit-load-<pid>-<random suffix>/` (the parent directories must be real directories, a symlink component is a refusal, as with the administrative directories of PROP-002), write every file of the package byte for byte with an atomic write, then rename the directory to `v<version>` (atomically within the parent; the target must not exist — it appeared between the check and the rename → a repeated classification: identical — the temporary directory is removed, otherwise `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`). **identical** → no file is written.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-NOTICE: Write the notice into both roots (`STD-NOTICE-TARGETS`) with an atomic write: the text is a render of the shipped template with the components block computed for this product **after** the package or the library has been written (`STD-NOTICE-COMPONENTS-BLOCK`); a copy already equal to the render is not rewritten; a copy that differs from the render only in the content of the block (another version of a component) is rewritten — that is not drift; any other difference is `drift`, refused earlier. Then remove the legacy copy `delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` when there is one (`STD-NOTICE-LEGACY-COPY`). The step is shared by `standards load` and `runtime load` (the function `writeNoticeCopies`).
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-MANIFEST: Write the manifest block by `STD-MANIFEST-STATE-MACHINE`; a file whose result is byte-identical to the original is not rewritten.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-SCRAPE: Write the scrape contract block by `STD-SCRAPE-STATE-MACHINE` (the prechecks `STD-SCRAPE-ENTRY-OUTSIDE-BLOCK` and malformed run at the step `STD-LOAD-STEP-MANIFEST-PRECHECK` together with the manifest — a refusal comes before any write); when there is no contract — `STD-SCRAPE-NO-CONTRACT`.
facts.STD-LOAD-STEP-REPORT: The summary: the package `(group, name, version)`, the source, the target, the files (`created`/`unchanged`), the copies of the notice (`created`/`unchanged`), the manifest (`appended`/`updated`/`unchanged`), the scrape contract (`appended`/`updated`/`unchanged`/`no-contract`), `otherVersions`, the licence line of the package (`licences loaded: UPL-1.0 (own, N files); MIT (third-party, M files); notices: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` — from the `LIC-CHECK-REPORT` report), the next command `vibe install --offline` (Codkit does not invoke vibe — `DECISION-STD-NO-VIBE-INVOCATION`); `--json`: `data: {package:{group,name,version}, source, target, files:{created,unchanged}, noticeFiles:[{path, action}], manifest:{path, action}, scrape:{path, action}, otherVersions:[…], removedScratch:[…], licences:{own, thirdParty, notices}, next:"vibe install --offline", notes:[…], recommendations:[…], noticeText?}`.
facts.STD-LOAD-LICENCE-NOTE: After the summary — on any outcome with exit 0, `up to date` and `--dry-run` included — the command prints a fixed licence note (owner decision of 2026-09-06: «вывести про это чёткую рекомендацию в консоли»), four lines, verbatim: `licence note: the package under vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/ carries its own LICENSE and REUSE.toml; they describe the package only.` / `licence note: this repository's own licence file is untouched and is never copied anywhere by codkit.` / `licence note: the fork tree's licence files and the product.json licence fields are upstream files - change them with a delta artifact in this patch set, never by hand.` / `licence note: a REUSE.toml for the fork tree is a delta artifact too.` Under `--json` the same lines are `data.notes: [...]`; in `messages` their level is `info`.

p.STD-LOAD-ALL-PACKAGES: **Every package the patch set is due in one run** — the universal set plus the packages its project type names (`STD-SHIPPED-PACKAGES`, `STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`): the steps of the source, the licence gate, the classification of the target and the write run for every package in turn, in the order of the names; a refusal of any package before the first write stops the whole run with nothing written; the managed block of `vibe.toml` is one, between the same markers, with one `[requires.packages."org.vibevm.codkit/<name>"]` table per package (the needle for a foreign entry is taken per name); the summary is per package; the `next:` lines are `vibe install --offline`, then `vibe skill install` when at least one delivered package declares a `[[skill]]`.

p.STD-LOAD-UPGRADE: `codkit standards load --upgrade` — when the target is in the `drift` state (or when another version of the same package is installed) it replaces the package directory as a whole on the explicit flag: the plan lists the `replace`/`remove` paths, the write goes through a temporary directory and a rename, and the copies of the notice and the manifest block are updated as in an ordinary delivery; without the flag `drift` stays a `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` refusal with the hint "run codkit standards load --upgrade to take the shipped copy, or move your edits out". A version directory of the same package other than the shipped one is **removed** by `--upgrade` and named in the plan as `<parent>/v<version>/` under `remove`, and in the report under `removedVersions`; a run without the flag keeps it and only lists it as `otherVersions`, so the move of the packages to the development version 1.0.0 (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0`) leaves `v0.2.0` and `v0.1.0` standing in a product until `--upgrade` is given. The form and the semantics are those of `runtime load --upgrade` (PROP-015 `RT-LOAD-UPGRADE`).

p.STD-LOAD-IDEMPOTENT: A repeat run after a success is a no-op: `identical` plus the block `unchanged`, `up to date` printed, exit 0, not one byte changed (the sha256 of the files before and after are compared). An interruption leaves either the temporary directory `.codkit-load-*` (removed by the next run) or a finished `v<version>` without the block (the next run appends the block) — the next command recognizes both states.

p.STD-LOAD-ROOTS: The command needs patchesDir and `codkit.json` (`configMode: 'load'`), and nothing else: the fork tree is neither required nor read, and the tree lock is not taken. The configuration is read for exactly one answer — the project type, and therefore which packages this patch set is due (`STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`) — so a patch set with no configuration is `CK-E-CONFIG` saying there is no project type to ask, exit 2, with nothing written; `standards check` refuses the same way, and `standards license` still needs no root at all. Under `--ci` the command is allowed (there is no network). Until the split of the packages per type the command read no configuration at all, and a patch set could load the standards before declaring what it forks.

p.STD-CHECK-ALGORITHM: Read-only, **for every package the patch set is due** (`STD-SHIPPED-PACKAGES`, `STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`): (1) the state of the target by `STD-LOAD-STEP-TARGET-STATE` — `absent` / `identical` / `drift` with the list; (2) `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` on the installed copy when there is one; (3) the state of both `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copies against the render with the current components block (`STD-NOTICE-TARGETS`), plus `legacy-copy` for the legacy path; (4) the state of the manifest block — `absent` / `current` (equal to the canonical one for the version of the package) / `stale` (present but different — another version, for example) / `malformed` / `entry-outside-block`; (5) the state of the scrape contract block — `no-contract` (information, not a finding) / `absent` / `current` / `stale` / `malformed` / `entry-outside-block`; (6) `STD-MANIFEST-TAIL-CAVEAT`; (7) `otherVersions`. Exit 0 only when the package and both copies are `identical`, the licence check is clean, the manifest is `current` and the scrape block is `current` or `no-contract`; 1 otherwise, every finding on its own line (`CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` for the target and the copies, `CK-E-LICENSE-*` for the copy of the package, `CK-E-CONFIG` for both blocks, the hint "run codkit standards load"; for a notice copy in the drift state the hint is "delete the copy and run codkit standards load"); 2 — the environment. `--json`: `data: {target:{state, paths}, license:{problems}, noticeFiles:[{path, state}], manifest:{state, path}, scrape:{state, path}, otherVersions}`.
