p.DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION: **Decision:** until an explicit word from the owner, the standards edition and the version of the runtime library are **mutable**: the content is extended in place under the same version number, the way the package manager itself does with its own packages at version 1.0.0 during development. **Why:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-07 («пока также следовать этой практике; когда нужно будет вернуться к честному перевыпуску — скажу явно»); a re-release for every change to young standards is version noise with no benefit. **Mechanics:** an installed copy whose bytes differ from the shipped ones is still `drift` for `standards check` (by the bytes the tool cannot tell an edit of the product from an update of the tool); `codkit standards load --upgrade` replaces the package directory as a whole on the explicit flag, like `runtime load --upgrade` (`STD-LOAD-UPGRADE`); then `vibe install --offline --force` rebuilds the projection. **Considered and rejected:** a silent replacement on `load` (loses the product's edits without a word); a forced version bump (contradicts the ruling). **The number:** owner ruling of 2026-09-08 fixed it at **1.0.0** for every package the tool ships - the standards edition, the agent skills and the runtime library - so the mutable content lives under one number instead of a number left over from the last honest release (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0` in the conventions; the directories `standards/v0.2.0`, `agent-skills/v0.1.0` and `runtime/v0.1.1` moved to `v1.0.0` with no change of content). **When to revisit:** an explicit instruction from the owner to bring re-releases back — then `THE-SET-IS-AN-EDITION` applies literally and `--upgrade` stays only for a change of version.

p.DECISION-STD-SKILLS-PACKAGE: **Decision:** the agent skills are a separate package `agent-skills` with `[[skill]]`, delivered by the same `standards load` and projected by `vibe skill install`; `packages/codkit/claude/skills/` is abolished. **Why:** VibeVM can already project skills into every harness (PROP-018 §2.6, `vibe skill list|install`), while a hand-written profile for one harness is a second source of the same procedure; the version of a norm must not change because a procedure was edited. **Considered and rejected:** the skills inside the standards package; a separate command `codkit skills load`; keeping `packages/codkit/claude/skills/` as the source and generating the package from it (the source must live where `vibe` reads it). **When to revisit:** VibeVM learns to project subagents/hooks (then `agents/` and `rules/` move into the package as well), or the `package` phase of the lifecycle becomes `impl`.

p.DECISION-STD-PACKAGE-IS-A-VIBE-FLOW:
**Decision:** the standards are an ordinary vibe package of kind `flow`, which lives in the `vibevm/vibepacks/` of toolRoot and in the `vibevm/vibepacks/` of the product, and is materialized by `vibe install` itself.
**Why:** the spike of 2026-09-06 in a scratch project: `vibe install --offline --assume-yes` found the package in `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v0.1.0/` without a `path` field, wrote `source_kind = "local"` into `vibe.lock`, copied the files into `vibevm/vibedeps/org.vibevm.codkit.standards/0.1.0/` byte for byte (the extensionless `LICENSE` and the XML header comment included), compiled the snippet into `STATIC.md`, `vibe check` — clean, a repeat installation — "re-copy skipped". Not one line of new machinery on the vibe side.
**Considered and rejected:** - copying the specifications straight into the product's `vibevm/vibespecs/` — they become the product's "own" files, get edited and diverge, and the anchors lose their provenance; - publishing the package to a registry and installing it with `vibe install org.vibevm.codkit/standards` — that needs a registry and a network; Codkit works without a network, and the edition must match the installed version of Codkit; - a git-source dependency — a network and a separate repository for the sake of one directory.
**When to revisit:** the package gains a consumer without Codkit (observed as a request to install it from a registry) — then publishing to a registry becomes a second delivery channel.

p.DECISION-STD-MANIFEST-BLOCK:
**Decision:** the dependency is written by a managed block between marker comments at the end of `vibe.toml`, by a byte scan, without a TOML parser.
**Why:** the same law as for the tree's `info/exclude` (`# codkit:begin managed`) and for the managed-blocks practice: one block, not a byte outside it, a deterministic search, no auto-repair. The form was checked with `tomllib`: the block appended at the end of a consumer manifest ending with a `[requires.packages]` table, and at the end of Codkit's own manifest ending with a `[[registry]]` element, gives a valid document in both cases, with `requires.packages["org.vibevm.codkit/standards"] = {version: "=0.1.0", link: "static"}`.
**Considered and rejected:** - parsing the TOML and reserializing it — loses the user's comments and order (`LIC-NEVER-REWRITE-THROUGH-A-PARSER`) and pulls in a dependency; - calling `vibe install org.vibevm.codkit/standards` — `DECISION-STD-NO-VIBE-INVOCATION`; - an inline key inside an existing `[requires.packages]` — the end of the table cannot be found without a parser.
**When to revisit:** vibe starts rejecting the dependency table after `[[registry]]` or demands another form of entry (observed as a red `vibe install` on a manifest that carries the block).

p.DECISION-STD-NO-VIBE-INVOCATION:
**Decision:** Codkit does not invoke `vibe`; `standards load` prints the next command, `vibe install --offline`.
**Why:** the NFR `NFR-SECURITY` — Codkit executes no foreign code apart from the npm build scripts; `vibe` may be absent from a CI container (PROP-011), and `--ci` forbids the network that `vibe install` without `--offline` may use. Two commands in a row are the price of one line in the report.
**Considered and rejected:** - a `--install` flag that runs vibe — a second road to the same result with new refusals (no vibe, the vibe version, the network); - writing `vibe.lock` and `vibedeps` ourselves — a duplication of vibe with a guaranteed divergence.
**When to revisit:** operators accumulate incidents of "forgot the `vibe install`" (observed through `standards check`, where the copy is there but the `vibedeps` slot is not — then `check` must learn to name that).

p.DECISION-LIC-THIRD-PARTY-NOW:
**Decision:** third-party files are supported from the first revision, in full, by the owner's document on licences: the allowlist and the exceptions in the policy, the `REUSE.toml` registry, the REUSE precedence of carriers, a `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` per licence, a generated `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` with a staleness check, the commands `license annotate` and `license notices`, the SPDX list.
**Why:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-06 on RP-4 of the campaign plan, verbatim: «реализовать все сразу по документу. для теста сгенерить какую-нибудь иконку для codkit и запиллтировать на ней». The pilot is a permanent fixture in the shipped package (`STD-PACKAGE-PILOT-ASSETS`): an own binary file with a sidecar and a real third-party file under MIT with a registry and notices; the reference implementation in Python and the oracle of 19 fixtures (`LIC-REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTATION`) give the worker checkable behaviour before the first line of TypeScript.
**Considered and rejected:** - revision 1 for own files only (the earlier decision of this anchor) — cancelled by the ruling; - the half-measure "a foreign file by its header without a registry" — without a registry there is no provenance and no notices, and the check stops being strict.
**When to revisit:** the first incident where `reuse lint` and `codkit license check` disagree in their verdict on one package (observed by the manual cross-check of `LIC-CHECK-CALLSITES`) — then the divergence is examined as a defect on one of the two sides.

p.DECISION-LIC-TOML-PARSER:
**Decision:** `REUSE.toml` is read by the library `smol-toml` (BSD-3-Clause, no dependencies; version 1.8.0 — the licence confirmed against the installed package on 2026-09-07), a new runtime dependency of Codkit; no parser of our own is written; `vibe.toml` and the scrape contract are still not parsed (the managed blocks are a byte scan).
**Why:** the registry is a foreign format (the REUSE specification), and the files come not only from us (`annotate` appends, a human edits); a strict parser of the full TOML grammar is not written in 200 lines without defects, and a weak worker is not able to find such a defect. Dependencies are allowed, permissive-only (`DEPENDENCIES-PERMISSIVE`); the licence scan of the closure is as for `imageset` (`DECISION-IMAGESET-PERMISSIVE-LICENCES`): the output goes into the campaign report.
**Considered and rejected:** - a subset of TOML by our own hands — a refusal on any unforeseen construct of a foreign file and hidden defects in parsing strings and escapes; - parsing `REUSE.toml` with regular expressions — the same risk without an honest name; - applying the parser to `vibe.toml` and to the contract as well — reserialization loses the comments and the order (`LIC-NEVER-REWRITE-THROUGH-A-PARSER`), and a byte scan is enough.
**When to revisit:** `smol-toml` goes 24 months without a release or changes its licence (observed in `npm-shrinkwrap.json`).

p.DECISION-LIC-SPDX-LIST-AS-DATA:
**Decision:** the list of SPDX identifiers is the data file `toolRoot/config/spdx-license-ids.json` (739 identifiers, list version `01b8052` of 2026-09-03) with a `CC0-1.0` sidecar, regenerated by a script from the SPDX `json/licenses.json`; not a constant in the code and not a network request.
**Why:** the list changes several times a year and a human must update it deliberately; a data file diffs and is reviewed, a constant in the code is not; the network is forbidden under `--ci` (`NFR-NETWORK`).
**Considered and rejected:** - the npm package `spdx-license-ids` — one more dependency for the sake of a single array, and its version lags behind the list; - downloading it during the check — the network is forbidden in CI.
**When to revisit:** an identifier that is absent from the list appears in the package (observed as `not an SPDX identifier` on a valid fresh identifier) — then a regeneration.

p.DECISION-LIC-HEADER-BLOCK:
**Decision:** copyright lines are read only from the block up to and including the `SPDX-License-Identifier` line (`LIC-HEADER-BLOCK-ENDS-AT-SPDX`).
**Why:** the reference run of 2026-09-06 on the shipped package: the table header line `| Path | Copyright | License | Source |` of `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (the ninth non-empty line) matched the regular expression of a copyright line as "the holder `| License | Source |`", and an own file became "third-party without an annotation". The same sample from §7.7 of the owner's document would have failed the same way in any implementation without the block-boundary rule.
**Considered and rejected:** - making the year mandatory on every copyright line — third-party lines without a year are legitimate under REUSE; - narrowing the window to N lines — twenty lines are needed for preludes and long headers; - requiring the word `Copyright` at the start of the line — the table header begins with it too, after `| Path | `.
**When to revisit:** a carrier in which the copyright line stands **after** the SPDX line (observed as a false `no copyright line`) — then the rule changes to "the block is the contiguous group of lines that contains the SPDX line".

p.DECISION-STD-PILOT-ASSETS:
**Decision:** the pilot assets are the Codkit logo (the icon and the mark without a background in SVG with a header, the 512 and 128 rasters in PNG with sidecars, all from one geometry by the script `tools/make-logo.py`) and one third-party Feather Icons icon (`package`, tag `v4.29.1`, MIT) with a registry and notices.
**Why:** the owner rulings of 2026-09-06 («сгенерить какую-нибудь иконку для codkit и запилотировать на ней»; «иконку сгенери прямо сейчас сама… нарисуй сразу хорошую, это будет логотип нашего продукта»). The mark carries the meaning of the tool — a delta held by markers — and reads from 512 down to 32 px (inspected on a contact sheet of 512/128/64/32/16). The own PNGs prove the "a binary file plus a sidecar" path and the copying of the pair by `standards load`; the third-party icon proves the "a registry plus the allowlist plus notices plus `LICENSES/MIT.txt`" path on a real foreign file; Feather is the example from the owner's document. The rasters are made with Pillow by supersampling from the same numbers as the SVG: `@resvg/resvg-js` is not installed in the Codkit checkout, and this machine's ImageMagick lost the contours (`fill="none"` plus `stroke`); one geometry for the SVG and the PNG rules out a divergence between them.
**Considered and rejected:** - own assets only — the third-party path would have been left without real bytes and a real foreign holder; - composing the mark from a Feather glyph — a file with two holders and the expression `UPL-1.0 AND MIT` complicates the classification for the sake of a picture; - rasterizing the SVG with an external tool — on this machine not one of them drew the contours correctly, and the version of the tool would make the bytes irreproducible.
**When to revisit:** the owner replaces the logo — then the assets and the sha256 in this anchor change in one commit, and the redrawing script with them.

p.DECISION-STD-LANGUAGE:
**Decision:** the standards package is English (the prose, the boot snippet, the README); the licence notice is bilingual, English and Russian; the UPL text is English only; the Codkit specifications stay Russian until a separate full translation into English; Codkit does not determine the language of a product's specifications.
**Why:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-06, verbatim: «Включить предупреждение о лицензии два раза - на русском и английском языке. Оригинальная лицензия UPL лежит в репозитории на английском языке. Пакет на английском языке.» and «Спеки Codkit мы в будущем переведем на английский язык целиком.» The package is the surface a product receives and may pass on; its licence is English, and a second normative language would be a second copy of every norm without a gate proving that the copies agree.
**Considered and rejected:** - Russian prose in the package (the first draft of the campaign) — cancelled by the ruling: the package is distributed, not only read by the owner; - bilingual specifications — two diverging copies; - writing PROP-014 in English right away — one English document among thirteen Russian ones breaks the convention of the repository; the translation is done in full by separate work.
**When to revisit:** at the full translation of the Codkit specifications into English (then PROP-014 moves together with all of them) and when a consumer of the package appears for whom English is not enough.

p.DECISION-LIC-ERROR-CODES:
**Decision:** three new codes — `LICENSE-HEADER` (a per-file carrier problem), `LICENSE-PACKAGE` (the consistency of the package), `STANDARDS-DRIFT` (the installed copy differs); problems of the manifest block use the existing `CONFIG`.
**Why:** the registry of codes is a unit of test coverage (`COVERAGE-ERROR-CODES`) and a row of the FAQ; one code per class of refusal keeps both lists readable, while the reason for each problem lives in the text of the message, as with `OVERLAY-SCHEMA`.
**Considered and rejected:** - a code per reason (no copyright, no SPDX, holder, orphan…) — seven codes without a machine consumer that would tell them apart; - one code `LICENSE` for everything — it mixes "fix the file" with "fix the package".
**When to revisit:** a machine consumer appears that branches on a specific reason (an `annotate` that repairs only "no header", for example).

p.DECISION-STD-TEMP-DIR-RENAME:
**Decision:** the files are written into the temporary directory `.codkit-load-*` and renamed to `v<version>` by one `rename`.
**Why:** the "identical/drift" classification of the target must not see half of the written files: an interrupted run that left `v0.1.0` with half its files would otherwise refuse with `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` against itself forever.
**Considered and rejected:** - writing straight into `v<version>` with an incompleteness marker file — the marker has to be removed last, and the window between removing the marker and the last write is there anyway; - counting a partial directory as drift and asking for a manual deletion — the tool must not ask anyone to repair what it left behind itself.
**When to revisit:** renaming a directory within its parent stops being atomic on any supported OS (observed as a flake of the e2e `standards.test.ts`).

p.DECISION-STD-NOTICE-FILE:
**Decision:** the Codkit licence notice is the file `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, which `standards load` places in the root of the product repository and in the root of the own code in the delta; it reaches the fork tree as an ordinary delivered own file, exempted from unit coverage.
**Why:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-06, verbatim: «я бы сделал чтобы файл с лицензией codkit копировался в корень <репозитория продукта>, и в корень "собственного кода" в дельте. Тогда он скопируется и в VSCode тоже автоматически. Назывался как-то типа LICENSE-CODKIT.md» (in the quotation the owner named the product; here the name is replaced with a placeholder — the tool repository carries no product names, and the substitution is marked rather than made silently). Delivery through the own root needs not one piece of new machinery: `load` already mirrors own into the tree, `ci`/`publish` already commit own; the only edit is one name in the "not own code" set of the manifest, so that `verify` does not require a unit.
**Considered and rejected:** - a resource-file layer — it needs an entry in the map with a guard test and a target that exists at the pin; the notice does not exist at the pin; - an add-file patch into the root of the tree — a patch for the sake of one file and a hunk that has to be carried over at every pin; - the product root only, without the own root — the file would not have reached the fork, and that is exactly what the owner wants.
**When to revisit:** the fork hygiene (`hygiene`/the pin lint) starts rejecting a `.md` in the own directory — observed as a red `ci --profile build` at the hygiene step with this path.

p.DECISION-STD-NOTICE-PRINT:
**Decision:** the recommendations are printed on every `standards load`; the full text of the file only in a run where a copy was created or updated, and always by the command `codkit standards license`.
**Why:** the owner ruling: «шаблон этого файла лучше 1) выдавать при выполнении установки пакета в консоли и 2) сделать команду codkit standards license которая печатает этот шаблон и рекомендации». The full text is almost two kilobytes of UPL; on a repeat `up to date` it would eclipse the summary, while the command gives it on demand at any moment.
**Considered and rejected:** - printing the full text always — noise on every repeat; the owner can bring it back with one flag of a decision, should they see fit; - not printing it at install time at all — contradicts the ruling.
**When to revisit:** the first incident of "the file was placed but no link was made, because nobody noticed" — then the full text is printed always.

p.DECISION-STD-SCRAPE-ROWS:
**Decision:** the rows of the `vibe scrape` contract that take `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` off a clean export are kept by Codkit in the product's `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` itself — in a managed block on every `standards load`; a contract is not created from scratch; for a contract at a non-standard path the rows are printed by `standards license`.
**Why:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-06, verbatim: «у продукта <продукта> может быть собственный контракт scrape, так что наше правило туда лучше вписывать алгоритмически» (the product name is replaced with a placeholder — the tool repository carries no product names). Checked live (`STD-SCRAPE-VERIFIED`): the block at the end of a contract created by `vibe scrape contract init` parses, `contract check` shows both copies under our rule and issues not one finding against our rows. The state machine of the block is the one of the manifest — one module for two files.
**Considered and rejected:** - printing the rows only (the first revision of this decision) — a product with a contract of its own edits it by hand, and the rows are forgotten; cancelled by the ruling; - creating the contract when it is absent — schema 1 requires `[health]` and at least one mandatory health check of the product, which Codkit does not know; without a contract there is no export anyway; - `proof = "sha256-v1"` with a `[[baseline]]` for both copies and `modified = "refuse"` — stricter (scrape would refuse to delete an edited copy), but the schema requires exactly one baseline per selected existing file, and the behaviour with an absent copy has not been checked; deferred (DEF in the plan) with the trigger below.
**When to revisit:** the first real `vibe scrape --in-place`/`--output` of a product (observed in the scrape report): if the export carried away an edited copy of the notice or refused on our rows — a move to `sha256-v1`; or an open extension table for packages appears in the contract schema.

p.DECISION-STD-NOTICE-RELEASE-EXCLUSION:
**Decision:** the `publish` release branch does not carry `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`; a clean export of the product repository through `vibe scrape` takes it off by the contract rows — both mechanisms, each on its own side.
**Why:** the owner ruling of 2026-09-06 on the question "the fork's release branch or the product's export": «сделать оба». The fork tree is a materialization of the patch set: a file deleted in the tree by a foreign tool would be read by `status`/`save` as work, and `load` would refuse over it; the release branch is built by `publish` from an immutable patch-set commit, so the only honest place for the exclusion is the own snapshot of the publication. The export of the product repository is the area of `vibe scrape`, and there the file is taken off by the contract (`STD-SCRAPE-CONTRACT-ROWS`).
**Considered and rejected:** - excluding it in `ci` as well — `ci` checks the developer's tree; `publish --profile build` repeats the profile of checks on the release build itself (PROP-007 §18), so the release bytes are checked where they are born; - deleting the file from the fork tree by running `vibe scrape --in-place` over the tree — a conflict with the ownership of the tree (`DRIFT-GUARD-PREDICATE`), plus a mutating scrape outside Windows refuses today (RP-10 of the plan); - not placing the file into `delta/own/` at all — cancels the ruling about delivering the notice into the fork.
**When to revisit:** `ci --profile build` starts counting as a release build (a profile that publishes artifacts appears) — then the option is switched on there as well; or upstream hygiene rejects a `.md` in the own directory (the trigger of `DECISION-STD-NOTICE-FILE`).

p.DECISION-STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS:
**Decision:** the scope of the notice is set by paths plus the generated components block and the paragraph about the vibe copies (`STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS`, `STD-NOTICE-COMPONENTS-BLOCK`, `STD-NOTICE-VIBE-COPIES`).
**Why:** a path covers files of any type without sidecars, is checked mechanically and is clear to a human; a static list of components lies as soon as the components become optional (a product with the library alone, a product with the standards alone); the compiled vibe lane lies outside the package directory and without an explicit reservation would contradict the rule by paths (owner decision of 2026-09-07).
**Considered and rejected:** - the reservation "the licence applies only if the files exist" — the licence applies only to what is in the copy anyway, and the reservation adds nothing; - recognizing the files by the header alone — impossible for images and data; - listing the components in prose — it goes stale at the first optional component.
**When to revisit:** a fourth delivery root appears.

p.DECISION-STD-NOTICE-UNDER-PREFIX:
**Decision:** the copy of the notice in the delta lies under the prefix `delta/own/codkit/`, the root copy stays; the legacy copy of edition 2 is removed by the delivering commands.
**Why:** one prefix is one truth about what belongs to Codkit; a `vibe scrape` export removes `vibevm/**` as a whole, so of Codkit's material only `delta/own/codkit/**` with its headers stays in the export, and excluding the notice from the release and from the export stays lawful.
**Considered and rejected:** removing the root copy — a reader of the repository needs it; keeping the copy at the own root — a second path for one thing.
**When to revisit:** together with `DECISION-STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS`.

p.DECISION-LIC-ANNOTATION-CARRIER:
**Decision:** a `REUSE.toml` annotation (a nested one included) is a carrier in its own right for files without a comment style; for source files the header is mandatory (`LIC-CARRIER-ANNOTATION`, `LIC-REGISTRY-NESTED`, `LIC-ANNOTATION-OWN`).
**Why:** a distribution carries hundreds of images and tables (a product's new interface), and a sidecar for each one is not the right form; the root of the fork tree belongs to upstream, so the registry of the own directory must be a nested one; a source file without a header stops being self-sufficient when a single file is copied.
**Considered and rejected:** a sidecar for every file as the only path; an annotation instead of a header in source files.
**When to revisit:** at a change of the REUSE specification.
